objectives: Put the sources of Bulgarian law in order, from the Constitution to a municipal ordinance.
Find the current text of a provision and check when it entered into force.
Read a citation such as "чл. 25, ал. 9, т. 1 ЗННД" and find it in the law library.
Explain the difference between legal capacity and capacity to act, between real rights and obligations, and between official and private documents.
Say when a contract is void and when it is voidable.

cards.front: Which act is the supreme law of Bulgaria?
cards.back: The **Constitution**; its provisions have direct effect ([[konst:5:1|Art. 5(1)]]–[[konst:5:2|(2) Конституция]]).

cards.front: When does a normative act enter into force if it says nothing?
cards.back: **Three days after promulgation** in the State Gazette ([[konst:5:5]]).

cards.front: What applies if a Bulgarian act contradicts an EU regulation?
Who sets the rate of the local tax on the acquisition of property?
cards.back: The **municipal council**, by ordinance, within the limits of the law ([[zmdt:1:2]]).

cards.front: What is the difference between "ал." and "т."?
cards.back: "ал." (алинея) is a **paragraph** of an article; "т." (точка) is an **item** inside a paragraph.

cards.front: Where are the definitions of an act usually found?
cards.back: In the **Additional Provisions** (Допълнителни разпоредби, ДР), numbered with §.

cards.front: A 17-year-old wants to sell her bicycle. Who signs?
cards.back: She signs herself, **with the consent** of a parent ([[zls:4]]); a small everyday deal needs no consent. Legal capacity (to hold rights) starts at birth ([[zls:1]]); capacity to act is full at 18 ([[zls:2]]).

cards.front: How does a minor aged 15 sign a contract?
cards.back: Personally, **with the consent** of a parent or curator ([[zls:4]]).

cards.front: What form does a contract for the transfer of real estate need?
What happens to a contract without the form required by law?
Name three grounds that make a contract voidable.
cards.back: Lack of capacity, mistake, fraud, threat, extreme need ([[zzd:27]]).

cards.front: Time limit to request annulment of a voidable contract?
cards.back: **Three years**, as a rule ([[zzd:32]]); **one year** for extreme need ([[zzd:33]]).

cards.front: What does an official document prove?
cards.back: The statements made before the official and the acts done by or before the official ([[gpk:179:1]]).
Land, plants, buildings and everything permanently attached to the land or a building ([[zs:110]]).

quiz.question: An ordinance of a minister contradicts a law. Which one applies?
options: The law
The ordinance, because it is newer
Both equally
The one chosen by the notary
quiz.explanation: [[zna:15:1]]: a normative act must agree with the Constitution and with every act of a higher level; an ordinance only implements the law that allows it ([[zna:12|Art. 12]]). The date of the act does not matter.

quiz.question: A law is promulgated on 10 March and says nothing about its entry into force. When does it enter into force?
options: 13 March
10 March
1 April
On the next 1 January
quiz.explanation: [[konst:5:5|Art. 5(5) of the Constitution]]: a normative act enters into force three days after its promulgation in the State Gazette, unless the act sets another term. 10 March plus three days is 13 March.

quiz.question: What does "чл. 8, ал. 1, т. 3 ЗННД" mean?
options: Article 8, paragraph 1, item 3 of the Notaries Act
Article 8, item 1, paragraph 3 of the Notaries Act
Chapter 8, article 1, item 3 of the Notaries Act
Paragraph 8, item 1, line 3 of the Notaries Act
quiz.explanation: "чл." is the article, "ал." the paragraph inside the article, "т." the item inside the paragraph; the act comes last. The order matters: paragraph 1, item 3 is not item 1, paragraph 3.

quiz.question: Which court hears an appeal against a notary's refusal to certify?
options: The regional court (окръжен съд)
The district court (районен съд)
The Supreme Administrative Court
The Notary Chamber
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:577:1]]: a refusal to perform a notarial certification is appealed with a private appeal before the окръжен съд, which this course calls the regional court. The district court houses the registration judge, who handles entries, not appeals.

quiz.question: Who orders an entry in the property register?
options: The registration judge
The notary
The mayor
The cadastre office
quiz.explanation: [[zsv:280]]: the registration judge at the district court orders or refuses entries, notes and deletions in the property register. The notary presents the act; the cadastre office issues sketches.

quiz.question: A 13-year-old inherits an apartment. Who signs a contract about it?
options: The parents, as legal representatives, in the child's name
The child alone, because an inheritance is a benefit
The child, with the consent of the parents in writing
Nobody; the apartment waits until the child turns 18
quiz.explanation: [[zls:3]]: a child under 14 cannot act; the parents act in the child's name. Consent of the parents is the regime of a minor from 14 to 18 ([[zls:4|Art. 4]]). A disposal of the child's real estate also needs the permission of the district court ([[sk:130:3]]; chapter 12).

quiz.question: A sale of a house is made in simple written form. What is its status?
options: Void for lack of the required form
Valid between the parties, not against others
Voidable within three years
Valid once entered
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:18]] requires a notarial deed for a transfer of real estate; [[zzd:26:2|Art. 26(2)]] makes a contract without the required form void. A void contract has no effect even between the parties, and an entry cannot cure it; only a preliminary contract in writing gives a claim for a final contract ([[zzd:19|Art. 19]]).

quiz.question: A person signed a contract because of a threat. What is the status of the contract?
options: Voidable
Void
Valid and unchallengeable
Non-existent
quiz.explanation: [[zzd:27]]: a contract concluded by mistake, fraud, threat or in extreme need is voidable; [[zzd:30|Art. 30]] defines the threat. The contract stands until a court annuls it at the request of the threatened party ([[zzd:32|Art. 32]]), unlike a void contract, which has no effect from the start.

quiz.question: Which statement about a private document is correct?
options: It proves that the signatories made the statements in it
It proves that the statements in it are true and complete
It has the same force as a notarial deed
It must always be made in notarial form
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:180]]: a private document signed by its authors proves that the statements were made by them, not that they are true. Only an official document proves the facts certified before the official ([[gpk:179|Art. 179]]).

quiz.question: Which right can its holder assert against a later buyer of the property?
options: A right of use created by an entered deed
A claim from a loan given to the former owner
An unentered promise of the owner to sell
A verbal permission to park in the yard
quiz.explanation: A real right, such as the right of use, acts against everybody (chapter 9); it is created by a deed and entered ([[zs:56]]). A loan, a promise or a permission is an obligation that binds only the parties ([[zzd:8]]); the buyer need not respect it.

quiz.question: Which source is the official text of a Bulgarian law?
options: The State Gazette
lex.bg
The website of the Notary Chamber
A commercial legal database
quiz.explanation: Only the State Gazette carries the official text; promulgation there starts the term for the entry into force ([[konst:5:5|Art. 5(5) of the Constitution]]). lex.bg and commercial databases offer consolidated texts, and the Chamber publishes guidance, not the law.

quiz.question: A deadline for filing an appeal at the court ends on Friday. Until when can you file it at the court office?
options: Until the end of the working hours on Friday
Until midnight on Friday, at the court office
Until Monday morning, the next working day
Until midnight on Sunday, by the court's e-mail
quiz.explanation: [[gpk:62:1]]: when something must be filed with the court, the term ends with the end of the working hours of the last day. Midnight applies only to filings sent by post or electronically ([[gpk:62:2|Art. 62(2)]]), not to a filing at the court office.
